Class Chances<T>

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.core.random.Chances<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the type of the outcomes
public final class Chances<T> extends Object
The exact chances of each outcome of something random: of each element that a RandomSelector selects, or of each multiset that a RandomTable draws. 
var rarity = RandomSelector.weighted(Maps.map("common", 70, "rare", 25, "legendary", 5));
var chances = rarity.chances();
chances.of("rare");                                      // 1/4
chances.where(name -> !name.equals("common"));           // 3/10
chances.outcomes();                                      // {common=7/10, rare=1/4, legendary=1/20}

Chances are computed on fractions of any size. A method that returns fractions throws ArithmeticException if one of them, in lowest terms, has a numerator or a denominator that doesn't fit in an int. The chances of weights that are whole numbers are simple fractions; a weight such as 0.1 is the double nearest to a tenth, which is a fraction of very large numbers.

Outcomes are told apart with equals and hashCode, and kept in the order they were given. Chances are immutable.

Since:
0.2.0

    • selector

      public RandomSelector<T> selector()
      Returns a selector that selects each outcome with its chance, and whose RandomSelector.chances() are these ones. It selects in the same time however the chances were computed.

      The selector rounds each chance to a double. Each selection calls RandomGenerator.nextLong() once, or what a uniform selector does if the chances are all equal.

      Returns:
      a selector of the outcomes
